# nf-claw

> A self-maintaining library of nf-core Nextflow (DSL2) pipelines for AI agents and bioinformaticians. Each pipeline is an unmodified git submodule pinned to a release, with a generated skill.md (how to run it) and reference.md (every parameter). The nfclaw command validates a run before launch, records a provenance bundle for replay, chains pipelines and serves all of this over MCP.

What an agent needs to know before using this repository:
- Finding a pipeline: run `nfclaw list <keywords>` (ranked matches) or grep `catalog.json` or `catalog.md`. Do not read the catalogs or directory listings whole.
- Reading it: `pipelines/<name>/skill.md` has the inputs, required parameters and run command of the pinned release; `pipelines/<name>/reference.md` has every parameter with its constraints.
- Running it: `nfclaw run <name> --input <file> --outdir <dir> -profile <profile>` (or `python3 -m runner run ...` from the repository root), with Python 3.11+. `--check` validates and prints the command without starting the pipeline; it leaves the output directory untouched but may initialise sources and run the engine to parse the configuration.
- No samplesheet yet: pass the data files as `--input` (a directory, a quoted glob, or `--input` once per file) and nfclaw writes the samplesheet from the pipeline's own schema. Set the columns no file name determines with `--sheet-set COLUMN=VALUE`; each `skill.md` lists them under Inputs.
- Following a run: `nfclaw status <outdir>` (`--json` for one object; same exit codes). The run log is `<outdir>/provenance/logs/run.log`. A lock file beside the output directory (`.<outdir name>.nfclaw.lock`) stops a second run into it.
- Sample identifiers: sample, patient and genome or database names must start with a letter, digit or underscore and contain only letters, digits, combining marks, dots, underscores and hyphens (Unicode letters and digits count). nfclaw refuses other identifiers rather than renaming samples. Local paths in a samplesheet must be absolute.
- Chaining: `nfclaw chain run <spec.json> --outdir <dir>` runs pipelines in sequence from a JSON spec.
- Replay and verification: `<outdir>/provenance/commands.sh` re-runs a run into a fresh directory after checking its sources, inputs and configs, then compares the execution environment with the recording and fails on detected differences. `nfclaw verify <target> --against <original>` compares the two runs.
- Scientific outputs: `nfclaw assess <outdir> --contract <file> [--against <original>]` checks declared outputs, parsed formats (BAM, VCF, FASTA, TSV, H5AD), sample coverage and numeric tolerances against a contract.
- MCP: `nfclaw mcp` serves the library and runner to MCP clients (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Hermes) on stdio; runs and chains become detached jobs, followed by job id (`docs/mcp.md`).
- Read `AGENTS.md` before running or chaining pipelines.

## Agent Guidance

- [Agent guide (AGENTS.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/AGENTS.md): How to find, run, follow, replay and chain a pipeline: commands, preflight, samplesheet rules, sample identifiers, status, locking, scientific assessment and which warnings are harmless.
- [Claude Code entry point (CLAUDE.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/CLAUDE.md): Imports AGENTS.md for Claude Code.

## Essential Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/README.md): What nf-claw does, repository layout, quickstart, provenance, scientific limits and citation.
- [Architecture (docs/architecture.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): The repository's parts, the runner's modules, preflight, output locking, provenance bundles, replay, verification and assessment.
- [Chaining (docs/chaining.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/chaining.md): Chain specs, handoff rules, retries, resume and lineage checks.
- [Engine compatibility (docs/compatibility.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/compatibility.md): Matching the Nextflow version to a release (`--nxf-ver`), passing `NXF_*` variables (`--nxf-env`), the CI workflows and host requirements.
- [Timeouts (docs/timeouts.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/timeouts.md): Optional deadlines, setup and shutdown margins, background runs and quick chain status.
- [Known issues (docs/known-issues.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/known-issues.md): Symptoms and fixes for host problems (IPv6, disk, permissions), runs, replays and chains, harmless Nextflow warnings and upstream pipeline bugs. Search it by section with the MCP `read_doc` tool.
- [Preflight (docs/preflight.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/preflight.md): Which checks run before launch, which are left to the pipeline, the samplesheet generator and the pipelines it supports, and what is refused before launch.
- [Replay and verification (docs/replay.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/replay.md): What a provenance bundle holds, what the replay checks before and after Nextflow runs, inputs that change during a run, resuming with changed inputs, and what `nfclaw verify` (`--strict`, `--require-environment`) and `nfclaw assess` show.
- [Scientific output contracts (docs/scientific-output-contracts.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/scientific-output-contracts.md): The contract format for `nfclaw assess`: formats compared (BAM, VCF, FASTA, TSV, H5AD), sample coverage and exact tolerances.
- [Source corrections (docs/source-corrections.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/source-corrections.md): The recorded corrections for Createtaxdb, Funcscan and Bactmap (applied to a separate copy of the source) and fastqrepair, and how they are replayed.
- [Publication policy (docs/maintenance.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/maintenance.md): What the maintenance workflows must show before they publish to main: one frozen candidate, the full test matrix, real runs checked from their raw traces, and retained artifacts.
- [DRAMP reference (docs/dramp-reference.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/dramp-reference.md): Preparing and indexing a DRAMP antimicrobial peptide reference for Funcscan.
- [Validation (docs/validation.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/validation.md): End-to-end runs of every pinned pipeline and of nfclaw's replay, resume, chain and stop handling; replays of every pipeline's provenance bundle; what passed, the settings each run needed, and what the evidence does not show.
- [MCP server (docs/mcp.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/mcp.md): Setting up `nfclaw mcp` in Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Hermes and other clients; its tools (each runs an nfclaw command); detached jobs that survive restarts; served skills and docs; and the protocol versions supported.
- [Updating and discovery (docs/updating.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/updating.md): How pins follow upstream releases, how new pipelines are added, update policies and the drift gate (`librarian.check_drift`).

## Pipeline Catalogs & Library

- [Pipeline catalog, Markdown (catalog.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/catalog.md): Every pipeline with its pinned version, input, output locations and description. Grep it; do not read it whole.
- [Pipeline catalog, JSON (catalog.json)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/catalog.json): For every pipeline: name, pinned version, description, summary, input, output locations, tools and the pipelines it can feed. Grep it; do not read it whole.
- [Sources (sources.tsv)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/sources.tsv): Each pipeline's upstream Git repository and update policy.
- [Pipelines (pipelines/)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/tree/main/pipelines): One directory per pipeline: the pinned code (`upstream/`), the agent instructions (`skill.md`) and every parameter (`reference.md`).

## Optional

- [Contributing (CONTRIBUTING.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): Adding pipelines and handoff rules, changing the maintenance code, tests, releases and documentation conventions.
- [Changelog (CHANGELOG.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): User-visible changes by release (1.0.0, and what is unreleased on main), newest first, by pull request.
- [Audit records (docs/audit/README.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/docs/audit/README.md): Dated audits and remediations with their evidence; they describe the repository on their own date, not its current behaviour.
- [Security policy (SECURITY.md)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/SECURITY.md): How to report a vulnerability privately, and what is in scope.
- [Website](https://bmds-tue.github.io/nf-claw/): Pipelines, parameters, documentation and the state of the automation, rebuilt from the repository.
- [Citation (CITATION.cff)](https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-claw/blob/main/CITATION.cff): How to cite nf-claw.
